items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear, but no exported API in encryption.go has a doc comment (NewEncryptor, LoadKey, EncryptWriter, DecryptReader, Config). The ~95-line decryptReader.Read has few comments. Terse names: `k`, `errEnc`, `curWriter`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: decryptReader.Read is about 95 lines and mixes buffering, chunk reading, HMAC and decryption. Validate and LoadKey repeat the per-source checks and salt decoding. The outBuf copy/reset block and the 'truncated data' error branches are copy-pasted. File is 477 lines, just under the 500-line cap.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Errors are wrapped with %w and checked. But EncryptWriter panics on cipher setup errors, and `payload := make([]byte, chunkLen)` trusts an unbounded uint32 from the stream, so a bad length prefix can force a ~4GB allocation. Magic numbers are inlined: pbkdf2 4096, salt minimum 16, key length 32.

items.name: Interface changes limited to the specified ones
items.name_zh: 接口变更仅限题目要求
items.evidence: Mandated signature changes are done and all callers updated; unencrypted output is unchanged. Extra changes: Validate now has a pointer receiver (`func (job *Job) Validate()`) and joins errors instead of returning the first; getDumper only runs when storages exist. New YAML keys `key_source` break the repo's lowercase style (`dbdriver`).
